newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Thirty die in Central African Republic fighting.
newsitem.headline: Thirty die in Central African Republic fighting.

text.p: The death toll from three days of fighting between disaffected soldiers and peacekeepers in the Central African Republic has risen to around 30, officials of the Central African Red Cross said on Sunday.
Around 70 people have been wounded in the fighting in the capital, Bangui, which began on Friday.
The Red Cross said it pulled its workers out of combat zones in the centre and west of the capital when fighting flared up on Sunday afternoon after a relatively calm morning.
The injured include five French nationals, who were hit on Saturday by two stray mortar bombs that fell on the French embassy compound.
Reports on Sunday spoke of a French soldier being among the injured, but this could not be confirmed by French sources either in Bangui or Paris.
Witnesses said French helicopters were flying over the city, and French soldiers were said to be patrolling near major crossroads but were not engaged in the fighting.
An African peacekeeping force has been deployed in the Central African Republic since a January 25 peace deal that ended a series of mutinies.

That deal, brokered by Mali's respected former military leader Amadou Toumani Toure included a plan to reintegrate the mutineers from the paramilitary gendarmerie into their units, but efforts to achieve this have failed.
Toure was due to arrive in Bangui on Sunday in an attempt to intercede again.

Mutinies in April and May 1996 began as protests over pay but became a movement to topple President Ange-Felix Patasse, a northern civilian elected in 1993. The third mutiny began in November and degenerated into ethnic bloodshed.
French troops, in the country under a defence pact, restored order after the last mutiny and then handed over to the peacekeepers.
The African force includes soldiers from Burkina Faso, Chad, Gabon, Mali, Senegal and Togo. A Senegalese soldier was among the first casualties of the flare-up on Friday.
